comparison: Perfect agreement on biphasic decay pattern (C10-C14). Both evaluations support the finding; OpenEval emphasizes the improved model fit (R²=44.18% vs 16.3%), while peer reviewers accepted it without challenge, noting consistency with prior literature.

Perfect agreement on ROC analysis results (C35-C38). Both evaluations support the reported AUC values and differential performance across reservoir measures. Peer reviewers acknowledged the pattern aligns with stronger associations for total versus intact reservoir.

Perfect agreement on clustering analysis (C39-C46, C114). Both evaluations support the identification of two distinct clusters with significant differences in reservoir and immune characteristics. Reviewers acknowledged this as part of the study's findings without challenge.

Divergent evaluations on decision tree models (C47-C49). OpenEval supports the findings as appropriately descriptive with reasonable accuracy. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, questioning the interpretability and value of categorical classification versus continuous measurement.

Divergent evaluations on ML prediction performance (C50-C52). OpenEval supports ~70% accuracy as modest but above chance with proper train-test splits. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, noting ML algorithms don't outperform classic methods and cannot reveal relationships that don't fundamentally exist.

Perfect agreement on null findings for sex/race (C56). Both evaluations support this negative result. Peer reviewers noted the male-dominated cohort could bias results but did not dispute the reported lack of significant differences.

Perfect agreement on speculative nature (C80-C82). Both evaluations rate these mechanistic hypotheses as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes they are reasonable but lack direct evidence; peer reviewers did not explicitly evaluate but noted the overall non-obvious relationship.

Strong agreement on LOCO analysis (C28-C32). Both evaluations support the identification of demographic and clinical variables as important covariates. OpenEval notes weak explanatory power is acknowledged; peer reviewers accepted findings without dispute.

Perfect agreement on CD127 differential pattern (C23-C25, C27, C113). Both evaluations support this finding as a notable exception. OpenEval emphasizes it as novel warranting investigation; peer reviewers acknowledged CD127 as a marker identified for further study.

Strong agreement on correlation findings (C53-C55, C92). Both evaluations support the results with acknowledgment of weak-to-moderate correlations (~0.3). OpenEval notes proper statistical rigor; peer reviewers explicitly noted the weak signal was acknowledged by authors.

Strong agreement on correlation patterns (C17-C22, C26 vs C17-C19, C21-C22, C24, C26, C110, C112). Both evaluations support these findings. OpenEval emphasizes statistical significance despite weak-to-moderate strength; peer reviewers acknowledged the overall pattern while emphasizing weak magnitude.

Divergent evaluations on interpretive conclusions (C105-C107, C110-C112). OpenEval supports these as appropriate synthesis with cautious inference. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about mechanistic interpretations, noting difficulty evaluating utility and the non-obvious relationship.

Strong agreement on study limitations (C90-C91, C93-C94). Both evaluations support the authors' acknowledgment of cross-sectional design, small sample size, and male-dominated cohort. Peer reviewers explicitly emphasized these same limitations.
